newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian government says no delay in election.
newsitem.headline: Croatian government says no delay in election.

text.p: The Croatian goverment on Tuesday rejected the opposition Social Liberal party's demand for a postponement of Sunday's presidential election after its candidate Vlado Gotovac was attacked at a campaign rally.

"The government could not accept Mr Gotovac's demand because there are no constitutional or legal grounds for it. The law on presidential elections does not foresee the possibility of setting new dates for electoral activities," a government statement carried by state radio said.
Gotovac's Social Liberal party (HSLS) called for a two-week delay after a Croatian army officer struck him on the head with a belt buckle at an election rally last week.
The 66-year old Gotovac, who suffered a concussion and neck injuries, was released from hospital on Sunday but doctors said on Monday he had to refrain from any activity and stay in bed.

The HSLS asked for both other candidates, President Franjo Tudjman and Zdravko Tomac of the Social Democrats, to stop campaigning until Gotovac was better. They said Gotovac should be allowed to add on days he has lost to lengthen his campaign.
Tudjman, 75, who led Croatia to independence from federal Yugoslavia in 1991, is widely expected to win outright in the first round with 60-70 percent of votes.
